event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, dated February 16 2021, sits well within the 0-3-year window after the March 2020 declaration of the COVID-19 pandemic, so Time-Decay permits high severity scores.  Alle’s Form 10-K repeatedly states that COVID-19 has already produced concrete, material impacts (factory shutdowns, supply-chain interruptions, $96 million impairments) and that management anticipates continued or even worsening effects on demand, liquidity, labour availability and cyber-security.  The language is largely specific and descriptive—naming geographies, functional disruptions, and quantifying losses—rather than boiler-plate.  Although a few sentences mention mitigation (facilities re-opened, health measures, financial flexibility), these do not eliminate the forward-looking uncertainty.  Overall, the disclosures portray an event that is both presently harming operations and carrying significant residual risk; therefore, evidence snippets generally receive high-medium to maximum scores, moderated only where statements are generic or include concrete mitigating offsets.

evidence_list.snippet: Our normal business operations have been, and are expected to continue to be, adversely impacted by the global COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicit acknowledgement of adverse impact already occurring (‘have been’).
States impact will continue, signalling persistent forward-looking risk.
Covers overall ‘normal business operations’, indicating breadth of effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly ties pandemic to past and future harm across operations with no mitigation, meriting a high recent-event score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Actions taken to help limit the spread of COVID-19, such as general public health decrees or other government mandates to restrict business activities and travel, avoid large gatherings or to self-quarantine, have impacted and will likely continue to impact our ability to carry out business as usual, including the temporary suspension of some of our operations, shortages in materials, reduction in customer demand, increased absenteeism, costs associated with operational changes and an extended period of remote work arrangements for some of our employees which could increase cybersecurity risks and other operational risks.

components.reason: Details multiple realised operational disruptions (suspensions, material shortages, absenteeism).
Identifies shifts to remote work and associated cybersecurity risk.
Uses phrasing ‘have impacted and will likely continue’, showing both realised and ongoing risk.
Covers demand reduction alongside supply issues, illustrating systemic exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly specific enumeration of current and future operational, supply-chain and cyber risks warrants a near-maximum score of 9.

evidence_list.snippet: This pandemic has also caused, and may continue to cause, disruption to our global supply chain and business operations, in addition to the various effects noted elsewhere within the risk factors contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

components.reason: Affirms actual disruption of global supply chain and operations.
Highlights that disruption may persist (‘may continue to cause’).
References breadth across ‘global’ operations, increasing gravity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows realised and potential supply-chain harm, but in somewhat generic terms, yielding a solid score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, this pandemic has led to changes in commercial real estate occupancy, increases in work-from-home arrangements, constraints on government and institutional budgets and an uncertain business climate, which have all contributed to declines and delays in new construction and renovation activity during 2020, including in many of the commercial and institutional construction markets we serve.

components.reason: Links pandemic to measurable demand-side impacts (declines/delays in construction activity).
Identifies specific behavioural shifts (work-from-home, occupancy changes) affecting markets.
Provides temporal anchoring—effects were seen ‘during 2020’, confirming realised impact.
Covers multiple end-markets, showing broad exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific demand shocks in core markets make this a strong piece of evidence, scoring 8.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, as a result of the global economic disruption and uncertainty due to the COVID-19 pandemic, interim impairment tests were performed on select goodwill and indefinite-lived trade name assets in the first quarter of 2020, resulting in impairment charges of approximately $96.3 million.

components.reason: Quantifies a large financial impact ($96.3 million impairment).
Directly attributes impairment to pandemic-driven disruption.
Represents realised, not hypothetical, loss.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: A concrete, sizeable, pandemic-driven impairment produces the maximum score of 10.

evidence_list.snippet: The continued spread of COVID-19 may have further adverse impacts on our business, operations, customer demand, supply chain, cash flow generation, financial position and liquidity and may also exacerbate other risks and uncertainties described in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

components.reason: Covers wide spectrum of potential harms (operations to liquidity).
Explicitly flags possibility of ‘further’ adverse impacts, showing open-ended risk.
Notes potential to exacerbate other disclosed risks, signalling compounding effects.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but non-quantified forward-looking risk statement earns a solid 6.

evidence_list.snippet: During the early months of the pandemic, we experienced temporary production shut-downs due either to government mandate or to help ensure employee safety, most notably in Italy and the Baja region of Mexico.

components.reason: Confirms actual factory shutdowns, a direct operational hit.
Cites specific regions, adding granularity and credibility.
Links shutdowns to both regulatory mandates and employee safety, highlighting external constraint.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised production stoppages with geographic details justify a high score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: If the on-going economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic proves to be more severe than estimated, the economic recovery takes longer to materialize or does not materialize as strongly as anticipated, this could result in further impairment charges in the future.

components.reason: Warns of additional impairments, extending financial risk horizon.
Connects severity and timing of economic recovery to balance-sheet impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking impairment risk is material but conditional, yielding a moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, our management is focused on mitigating the impacts of COVID-19 which has required, and will continue to require, a large investment of time and resources, which may divert attention and resources from other business matters.

components.reason: Highlights organisational strain and resource diversion due to pandemic response.
States requirement will ‘continue’, stressing ongoing cost.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Resource diversion is noteworthy but less severe than financial losses, so the snippet scores 3.
